memories.subject: Coach House Wing roof leak discovered above the bar ceiling
memories.body: During the wet spell in late October, FOH staff reported water pooling behind the bar in the Coach House Wing, the 1890s extension that houses the bar and two dressing rooms. Hallam Roofing surveyed on 4 November and found slipped slates and rotten flashing around the valley gutter, estimated repair cost £38,000. Because the building is Grade II listed, any repair needs listed building consent from the district council conservation officer before work starts, adding at least six weeks. General Manager Priya Sanghera has applied to Arts Council England's Capital Kickstart fund for £25,000 towards the cost, with the theatre finding the remaining £13,000 from reserves. Interim buckets and a tarpaulin are in place until scaffolding goes up in January.

memories.subject: Casting confirmed for the Christmas production of The Tempest
memories.body: Artistic Director Neil Ashworth has cast the resident company's five permanent members plus three guest actors for The Tempest, opening 6 December and running to 18 January in the main 340-seat house. Prospero will be played by long-serving company member Douglas Fenn, Miranda by newcomer Aisha Okonkwo, straight from RADA. Designer Beth Callow is building a raked, sand-covered stage which requires the trap room floor to be reinforced, a job scheduled for the dark week beginning 10 November. Ticket prices range from £14 to £29, with a relaxed performance on 4 January and a BSL-interpreted show on 11 January. Marketing has budgeted £4,200 for print and social promotion, aiming to beat last year's panto attendance of 6,100.

memories.subject: Bar takings down after three-week closure of the Coach House Wing
memories.body:
The bar, based in the Coach House Wing, had to close entirely from 8 to 29 November while scaffolding went up for the roof repair identified after the leak above the bar ceiling. Catering manager Colin Marsh estimates lost bar and ice-cream kiosk revenue at around £6,500, based on average takings during the autumn studio season. A temporary trestle bar was set up in the foyer for evening performances only, staffed by two casual bar staff instead of the usual four, cutting interval service time in half and prompting several complaints logged in the front-of-house diary. Colin has asked the board to consider compensating the catering budget from the roof contingency fund once the Arts Council capital application outcome is known.

memories.subject: Saturday Youth Theatre numbers rise after new intake in September
memories.body: The Saturday Youth Theatre, run by youth and education officer Naomi Platt, now has 47 members across three age bands (7-11, 12-15, 16-18), up from 31 last year following a recruitment push in local primary schools. Sessions run 10am-1pm in the rehearsal room above the workshop, with termly fees of £45, though 9 members are on bursaries funded by the Hamilton Trust. The autumn term is building towards a devised piece about the town's Victorian mill history, to be performed in the studio on 14 December, tickets £5. Naomi has taken on a part-time assistant, Josh Kaye, 20 hours a week, to help manage the larger 16-18 group, who are also devising a separate piece for the youth arts festival in Leeds next March.

memories.subject: Touring co-production of Hobson's Choice heads to four venues
memories.body: The autumn touring production of Hobson's Choice, co-produced with Dale Street Theatre in Rochdale, opens at Harrowgate on 2 October before touring to the Palace Theatre Mansfield, the Forum Barnsley, and the Old Rep Alnwick, closing 9 November. Director Fran Ollerton has kept the cast to six, doubling roles to fit a small touring set designed to fit into a single 7.5-tonne van. The tour is supported by a £12,000 Arts Council touring grant plus a £3,000 contribution from each receiving venue. Get-in at each venue is a single day, with the technical stage manager, Ruth Iqbal, travelling with the company throughout. Harrowgate's own box office reports advance sales of 210 tickets for the home dates, slower than hoped, partly attributed to the show clashing with the town's harvest festival weekend.

memories.subject: Board treasurer questions reserve levels after roof spending discussion
memories.body:
At the November board meeting, treasurer Alan Whitmarsh raised concerns about the theatre's free reserves falling below the recommended three months' operating costs, currently around £74,000, after the finance sub-committee discussed the likely £13,000 shortfall on the Coach House Wing roof repair not covered by the Arts Council capital application. Alan proposed a formal reserves policy be adopted at the January meeting, requiring board sign-off before any reserve is used for capital works over £5,000. Chair Margaret Dunwoody agreed to circulate three years of management accounts ahead of that meeting. Alan also asked General Manager Priya Sanghera to bring quarterly cash-flow forecasts to every board meeting rather than the current twice-yearly reporting, a change the board approved unanimously.

memories.subject: New ticketing system Spektrix replaces ageing box office software
memories.body: Box office manager Denise Corrigan oversaw the switch from the fifteen-year-old Theatron system to Spektrix in August, at a cost of £9,600 for the first year including staff training. The change was driven by repeated crashes during the panto on-sale last December, which locked out phone bookings for two hours on the busiest sale day. Spektrix's customer relationship features let the theatre track that 62% of the 2,300-strong mailing list are repeat bookers, and a new £2-off scheme for under-26s launched in September has already sold 340 tickets. Denise has trained four box office volunteers on the new till interface, and average transaction time is down from 3 minutes to under 90 seconds, easing queues at the single foyer box office window.

memories.subject: Front-of-house team short-staffed after two ushers left in September
memories.body: FOH supervisor Gary Nield lost two long-serving volunteer ushers in September, one relocating for work and one retiring after eleven years, leaving the rota reliant on just six regular volunteers for a 340-seat house that needs eight per full house. Gary has recruited three new volunteers through a local Facebook community group and the theatre's own newsletter, with induction sessions held on 15 and 22 October covering fire evacuation procedure and the relaxed-performance protocol. Paid duty manager hours have had to increase temporarily to cover gaps, adding roughly £180 a week to the staffing budget through November. Gary is also proposing a small honorarium of £10 per shift for volunteers who cover last-minute gaps, to be discussed at the next staff meeting.

memories.subject: New Artistic Director Priya Chandrasekaran appointed for January 2025 start
memories.body: The board's appointments panel confirmed on 14 October that Priya Chandrasekaran will succeed Martin Ferris as Artistic Director, taking up the post on 6 January 2025 after a four-month handover. Chandrasekaran, previously an associate director at Northern Stage, was chosen from a shortlist of five following two rounds of interview and a 20-minute pitch to staff and board members on her first-season priorities: more new writing, a co-commissioning relationship with West Yorkshire Playhouse, and a push to raise the proportion of northern-based actors in the resident company. Her salary was set at £48,000, within the band agreed by the remuneration sub-committee. Ferris will remain as a consultant director for the already-programmed Tempest until March to ensure continuity.

memories.subject: Chandrasekaran's first programming choice is a new Alan Bennett-style monologue evening
memories.body:
As her opening statement of intent, incoming Artistic Director Priya Chandrasekaran has chosen to open her first season not with a large-cast classic but with an evening of three new monologues, working title 'Market Town Voices', to be developed with local writers over the winter. She has asked the literary associate to run open submissions from November, with a £500 commission fee per writer drawn from the existing script development budget. Casting will favour resident company members rather than guest actors, partly to keep costs low while she assesses the ensemble she has inherited. Staff have noted this is a marked change of direction from Martin Ferris's classics-led programming, and box office is nervous about audience appetite for unfamiliar new work in the 340-seat house.

memories.subject: Grade II listed façade stonework needs repair on the Market Street elevation
memories.body: The quinquennial building survey commissioned from Hartley & Boyce Conservation Architects has flagged spalling sandstone on three window surrounds along the Market Street façade, the theatre's original 1887 frontage, which is Grade II listed. Because the building is listed, any repair requires Listed Building Consent from the district council before work starts; the application was submitted on 3 September and a decision is expected within eight weeks. Estimated cost of the stone repair, using lime mortar and matched sandstone from a Yorkshire quarry, is £34,000, to be split between the maintenance reserve and a possible heritage grant application to the National Lottery Heritage Fund. The general manager has warned the board this sits on top of the Coach House Wing roof spending already agreed this year.

memories.subject: Stonemason contractor Denby & Sons delayed by autumn weather on the façade job
memories.body:
Denby & Sons, the conservation stonemasons awarded the Market Street façade contract after Listed Building Consent was granted in late October, have pushed their start date back twice, citing scaffolding hire delays and a run of wet weekends that make lime mortar work unsafe. Original completion was pencilled in for early December; it is now unlikely before late January, which the building manager says risks clashing with the busy panto period when scaffolding access along the front elevation would obstruct queuing patrons. Denby & Sons have agreed to work only Monday to Thursday during the show's run to keep the main entrance clear. No cost variation has been requested yet, but the general manager expects a claim for the extended scaffold hire period.

memories.subject: Arts Council England confirms 9% uplift in National Portfolio funding for 2024-27
memories.body: Arts Council England's decision letter, received 1 November, confirms Harrowgate Repertory Theatre's National Portfolio grant will rise from £412,000 to £449,000 a year for the 2024-27 investment period, a 9% uplift attributed largely to the strength of the youth engagement data submitted in the application and the theatre's touring track record. The letter specifically praises the partnership model behind the Hobson's Choice co-production and asks for continued reporting on audience diversity figures. The finance sub-committee has earmarked the additional £37,000 for a part-time audience development officer post rather than absorbing it into general reserves, a decision the treasurer supports as it creates a measurable outcome for the next funding review in 2027.

memories.subject: Bar switches coffee and soft drinks supplier from Nestlé Professional to local roaster Fox & Bean
memories.body: From 1 October the front-of-house bar changed its coffee supply from a Nestlé Professional contract to Fox & Bean, a roastery based twelve miles away in Ripon, after repeated complaints on comment cards about machine coffee quality during matinee intervals. The new arrangement costs slightly more per kilo but includes free machine servicing and staff training, which the catering manager expects to offset breakage and downtime costs seen with the old machine. Fox & Bean have also agreed to supply branded cups for the foyer café counter at no extra charge as part of a wider sponsorship conversation, and their name now appears on the programme's supporter page alongside the printers and the taxi firm used for late get-outs.

memories.subject: Trustee Margaret Iqbal resigns citing time pressures after eleven years on the board
memories.body: Margaret Iqbal, who has served as a trustee since 2013 and chaired the audience development sub-committee for the last four years, submitted her resignation on 20 September citing increased demands from her day job and a wish to make space for newer voices on the board. Her departure leaves the board with nine members against a constitutional minimum of seven, and the chair has asked the nominations panel to prioritise recruiting someone with digital marketing or fundraising experience given the gap her departure leaves in audience development oversight. Iqbal has offered to stay involved informally as a mentor to whoever takes on the sub-committee chair, and will be thanked publicly at the December board meeting alongside a small gift from the general fund.

memories.subject: Relaxed performance trialled for the Saturday matinee of the winter touring show
memories.body: On 7 December the theatre will trial its first relaxed performance, adapting the visiting touring production's Saturday matinee with house lights kept low rather than off, sound levels reduced for the storm sequence, and a chill-out space set up in the Ellis Wing rehearsal room for anyone needing to leave the auditorium. Front-of-house staff have had a short briefing session run by a visiting access consultant from Attitude is Everything, and visual story guides have been emailed to the four special school groups who have already booked. The touring company agreed to the adaptations without extra fee, though the stage manager has asked for confirmation in writing before the get-in that no lighting or sound cues will need altering mid-run for other performances in the venue.

memories.subject: Rehearsal clash between Bennett-style monologue evening and panto get-in
memories.body: Priya Chandrasekaran's first production, a five-hander monologue evening titled 'Waiting for the Kettle', was booked into the Ellis Wing rehearsal room for the last week of November, only to discover the room was already committed to the pantomime 'Jack and the Beanstalk' get-in, scheduled by the previous season's paperwork. Both companies needed the space simultaneously: monologue cast for blocking, panto crew for flying scenery tests. Chandrasekaran raised it directly with Production Manager Dave Holt on 14 November after her stage manager flagged the double-booking in the weekly schedule meeting. The clash threatened to push her opening back by four days, which would have collided with the Christmas Tempest previews already selling well.

memories.subject: Dave Holt reshuffles Ellis Wing schedule to save monologue evening opening
memories.body:
Following the Ellis Wing double-booking, Production Manager Dave Holt moved the monologue evening's blocking rehearsals into Studio 2 for the affected week, running 6pm-10pm slots rather than daytime, since Studio 2 was only used for youth sessions on Saturdays. This required paying an additional £180 in evening heating costs, as Studio 2's ancient radiators take two hours to warm the room, and extending caretaker Ron Pickersgill's hours by six hours across the week at time-and-a-half. Holt logged the decision in the production diary on 15 November, noting the panto get-in in the Ellis Wing was untouched and Chandrasekaran's opening date held at 3 December. He recommended the master rehearsal calendar be centralised to avoid repeat clashes next autumn.

memories.subject: Th'Real Ale Co. signs £8,000 season sponsorship deal for the bar
memories.body: The theatre signed a one-year sponsorship agreement with Th'Real Ale Co., a brewery based six miles away in Ripon, worth £8,000 plus stock discounts, replacing the previous informal arrangement with a regional cask supplier. The deal, negotiated by Bar Manager Colette Fry and signed off by the board's finance subcommittee in September, includes branded pump clips, a tasting event in the foyer on 12 October, and logo placement in the programme for all mainhouse productions this season. In return the brewery gets naming rights on the interval bar and first refusal on future festival sponsorship. Fry expects the deal to offset some of the takings lost during the Coach House Wing closure earlier in the year, though she flagged installation logistics as untested before opening night.

memories.subject: Cellar adaptor problem delays Th'Real Ale Co. kegs going on tap
memories.body:

A brass adaptor had to be sourced urgently from a Leeds catering supplier at a cost of £450, delaying the first pour by three days and pushing the tasting event back from 12 to 15 October. Bar Manager Colette Fry noted in her report to the board that the sponsorship deal's projected first-month revenue would be lower than forecast as a result, and recommended future supplier changes include a cellar compatibility check before contracts are signed.

memories.subject: Youth Theatre director Sian Vaughan hires assistant tutor Marcus Webb
memories.body: With Saturday Youth Theatre numbers up sharply after the September intake, director Sian Vaughan secured funding through the youth programme budget to hire an assistant tutor, appointing Marcus Webb, a recent drama graduate from the University of Leeds, on a part-time contract from October. Webb's role covers the under-12s group, which had grown from twelve to twenty-one members, too large for Vaughan to run alone alongside the teens' session. His salary, £4,200 for the academic year, comes from the same Arts Council-supported youth strand that funds scripts and materials. Vaughan reported to the board's education subcommittee that the extra pair of hands has already improved retention, with only one dropout since Webb started, compared to four in the previous term.

memories.subject: Marcus Webb launches teen devising strand 'Untold Histories' in Studio 2

Sian Vaughan approved the strand as a way to give Webb creative ownership beyond the under-12s group he was hired for, and it has attracted six new teen members who joined specifically for the project. memories.subject: Board recruits new trustee with finance background after governance review

Forty-one applications were received; the recruitment panel, chaired by vice-chair Howard Lister, shortlisted five and appointed Priti Sharma, a semi-retired chartered accountant from nearby Ripon, starting in March 2025. Sharma's brief specifically includes reviewing reserve policy and capital project reporting, an area the treasurer had flagged as under-scrutinised. memories.subject: Touring van breakdown strands set for the Hobson's Choice co-production
memories.body: The touring van carrying set flats and props for the Hobson's Choice co-production broke down on the A1 near Wetherby on 3 October, en route to the second of its four venues, causing a five-hour delay to the get-in at the receiving theatre. The RAC recovery cost £310 and the touring producer, Anna Ferreira, had to hire a replacement Luton van overnight from a Leeds firm at short notice for £180 to keep the schedule on track. The delay meant the technical rehearsal was cut from four hours to ninety minutes, which stage manager Joe Prentice said left several scene changes under-rehearsed for the opening night. Ferreira has since asked the tour's booking agent to build a half-day contingency into future transfer schedules.

memories.subject: Bar refurbishment budget approved for new till points and signage

The work is scheduled for the first week of January 2025 during the post-panto dark week, chosen to minimise disruption to trading. General Manager Alison Rees will project-manage, using local firm Hartley Joinery, who quoted £9,200 for the counter and shelving, with the remainder covering electrical work for the new tills. The refurbishment was prompted partly by customer feedback cards noting the bar looked tired, and partly by the need to accommodate the new Spektrix-linked card readers. Rees confirmed insurance won't need updating as no structural walls are affected.

memories.subject: Denby & Sons finally complete Market Street façade repair, invoice overrun
memories.body:
Denby & Sons finished the stonework repair on the Market Street elevation on 3 December, six weeks later than the original September estimate, after the autumn weather delays reported earlier. The final invoice came in at £31,400 against a quoted £26,000, with the £5,400 overrun attributed to additional scaffolding hire weeks and replacement of two more mullions than originally surveyed, which had deteriorated further while work was paused. Building manager Colin Pratt signed off the invoice but flagged it to the board's finance subcommittee, since it eats into the contingency set aside from the Arts Council uplift. Denby & Sons have offered a 5% discount on any future listed-building work as goodwill, which Pratt has noted for the next façade phase around the clock tower.

memories.subject: Th'Real Ale Co. kegs finally connected after three-week cellar delay
memories.body:
The cellar adaptor fault that held up Th'Real Ale Co.'s kegs going on tap was resolved on 14 October when cellar technician Greg Foulds sourced a replacement Sankey coupler from a Leeds supplier, after the original part ordered from the brewery's own supplier proved incompatible with the Harrowgate cellar's older lines. The sponsored ales — a bitter and a pale ale — went on sale for the opening night of the winter touring show, three weeks later than planned under the £8,000 season sponsorship deal. Th'Real Ale Co.'s rep, Joe Tansey, visited to check the pour quality and agreed to extend branded pump clips into the foyer bar as informal compensation for the delayed launch, which bar manager Alison Rees welcomed given lost early takings.

memories.subject: Volunteer usher scheme launched to plug September staffing gap
memories.body: Following the loss of two experienced ushers in September, Front of House Manager Denise Corrigan has launched a volunteer usher scheme offering free tickets to two shows per month in exchange for a minimum of six shifts. Twelve people attended an induction evening on 12 November, run in the Studio 2 rehearsal space, covering fire evacuation procedure, ticket scanning on the new Spektrix handhelds, and bar-carrying rules for interval drinks. Corrigan hopes to have eight volunteers regularly rota'd by the Christmas production of The Tempest, when audience numbers are expected to strain the current staffing level. Two paid part-time usher posts remain unfilled and are being advertised locally, with interviews planned for early December before the panto season begins.

memories.subject: Untold Histories showcase in Studio 2 draws unexpectedly large audience
memories.body:
The first public showcase of Marcus Webb's teen devising strand Untold Histories took place in Studio 2 on 23 November, with fourteen young people aged 13-17 presenting three short devised pieces on local mining history, migration, and mental health. Around 70 parents, carers and community members attended across two sharings, more than double what Sian Vaughan had anticipated when booking the space. Webb has asked for the showcase to move to the main house for the spring edition, citing demand, though this would clash with get-in for the spring touring production. Vaughan is raising the scheduling question with the artistic director's office. Feedback forms were overwhelmingly positive, with several parents asking whether Untold Histories could run as a paid public ticketed event next term.

memories.subject: Spektrix data migration glitch causes duplicate bookings during panto on-sale
memories.body:
When panto tickets went on general sale on 4 November, the new Spektrix system briefly double-booked eleven seats in rows F and G due to a data migration error carried over from the old box office software, which had not fully released held seats from a September group booking. Box office supervisor Neil Ashworth caught the issue within two hours after customer complaints and manually reseated affected bookings, upgrading three parties to better seats by way of apology. Spektrix's support team confirmed the fault lay in a legacy hold flag and pushed a patch on 6 November. Ashworth has since run a full seat-map audit ahead of Tempest tickets going on sale, to avoid a repeat during the Christmas period when box office volume is highest.

Follows from [[7]].

memories.subject: Fiona Marsh appointed trustee to replace Margaret Iqbal, finance focus
memories.body:
The board confirmed Fiona Marsh, a retired regional finance director, as the new trustee filling the vacancy left by Margaret Iqbal's resignation after eleven years' service. Marsh was recruited through the governance review process and formally joined at the December board meeting, where she was immediately asked to sit on the finance subcommittee alongside treasurer Alan Whitfield. Chair Deborah Snell noted Marsh's background auditing charity accounts made her well placed to scrutinise reserve levels, a topic Whitfield raised following the roof spending earlier in the year. Marsh has requested sight of the last three years' management accounts before her first full subcommittee meeting in January, and has already asked pointed questions about the Denby & Sons overspend on the façade contract.

memories.subject: Studio 2 heating fault reported ahead of winter youth theatre sessions
memories.body: Caretaker Bob Ellison logged a fault with the Studio 2 space heater on 28 November after Saturday Youth Theatre participants complained of cold during the 6-8pm session, with the room reading 11°C despite the thermostat set to 18°C. An electrician from Marsh & Kelt Ltd inspected on 2 December and found a failed relay in the storage heater unit, quoting £340 for a replacement part with a two-week lead time. In the meantime, Ellison has arranged two portable oil-filled radiators borrowed from the wardrobe department to keep sessions running. Sian Vaughan asked whether the studio's heating could be prioritised in next year's maintenance budget given the room now hosts both Saturday Youth Theatre and Marcus Webb's Untold Histories rehearsals on overlapping evenings.

memories.subject: Damp discovered in Ellis Wing dressing room 3 during Tempest fittings
memories.body: Wardrobe supervisor Jan Fetherstone reported black mould creeping along the skirting in Ellis Wing dressing room 3 on 14 October, likely linked to the same rainwater ingress that's plagued the wing since the Coach House Wing roof works began next door. Costumes for three Tempest cast members had to be pulled and dry-cleaned as a precaution. Building manager Dave Holt taped off the room and ordered a dehumidifier from Screwfix, but says a proper damp survey can't happen until the façade scaffolding comes down. Estimated repair cost unknown pending survey; Jan has asked for it to be prioritised before panto get-in in November, since three more dressing rooms share the same external wall.

memories.subject: Costume store temporarily relocated out of Ellis Wing dressing room 3
memories.body:

It's a squeeze — the rail barely fits between the shelving and the fire door — and Jan has flagged it as a fire-safety concern to Dave Holt. Two dressers have complained about lost floor space for steaming and pressing. The move is meant to be temporary until the damp survey, but Jan warns that if it drags into panto rehearsals in November there won't be room for both shows' costumes at once.

memories.subject: Project grant application submitted for new outreach scheme Market Town Voices
memories.body: General manager submitted an Arts Council England Project Grant application on 3 October for £15,000 to fund Market Town Voices, a six-month oral history and verbatim theatre scheme working with residents over 70 across the district's outlying villages. The bid was written jointly with the youth programme team, building on goodwill from the 9% National Portfolio uplift confirmed earlier this year. Budget covers a part-time community producer (0.4 FTE for six months), transport for participants, and a small-scale sharing in the Studio. Decision expected by late January. If unsuccessful, the scheme will be shelved rather than part-funded from core budget, given pressure on reserves.

memories.subject: Market Town Voices grant awarded at reduced level of £9,000
memories.body:
Arts Council England wrote back on 22 January offering £9,000 against the £15,000 Market Town Voices bid, citing high demand across the region's Project Grant round. The general manager and youth team met to rescope: the community producer post drops to 0.25 FTE, the outlying-village transport budget is cut entirely, and participants will instead be bussed in twice monthly to the main building. The Studio sharing survives but moves from a fully staged reading to a simple table reading. Board members raised concerns at the February meeting that a scaled-back version risks disappointing the elderly participants already recruited through the library service, but agreed it was better than cancelling outright.

memories.subject: Resident actor Grace Oduya signs three-year company contract extension
memories.body: Grace Oduya, with the company since 2019, signed a three-year contract extension in September covering four productions a year plus availability for the Hobson's Choice-style touring co-productions. Her rate rises from £520 to £580 per week, agreed by the board's finance sub-committee as part of efforts to retain experienced company members ahead of Priya Chandrasekaran's first season. Grace will lead the Bennett-style monologue evening and take a principal role in the Christmas Tempest. Casting director Alison Brook says retaining her removes the need to recast three roles that would otherwise have gone to freelance actors at higher weekly rates once agent fees are included.

memories.subject: Grace Oduya's touring dates clash with her monologue evening rehearsal block

memories.subject: Cellar cooling unit fault causes real ale wastage overnight in November
memories.body: The cellar cooling unit failed overnight on 11 November, and by the time bar manager Colin Riggs opened up at 10am two firkins of guest ale had risen above 14°C and had to be tipped — a loss of roughly £180 in stock. Colin called an emergency callout from Northern Refrigeration Services, who replaced a failed thermostat sensor for £310 including parts. Colin has asked the board's bar sub-committee to consider a service contract rather than reactive callouts, noting this is the third cooling issue in eighteen months. The wastage was absorbed into the bar's contingency line rather than reported separately in October's takings figures.

memories.subject: AGM set for 4 March with concerns over trustee attendance levels
memories.body: The board confirmed the AGM date of 4 March at the November meeting, to be held in the main house before a public Q&A with Priya Chandrasekaran about the coming season. Chair Robert Aldous raised concerns that only six of nine trustees attended the last two ordinary meetings, partly due to the gap left by Margaret Iqbal's resignation and partly clashing work commitments among newer members. Company secretary will circulate the AGM papers three weeks early rather than the usual two, in hopes of improving preparation and attendance. Papers will include the annual accounts, the Arts Council funding update, and a proposal to formally adopt a reserves policy following the earlier treasurer's questions about roof spending.

memories.subject: Stage Electrics wins tender for new Main House LED lighting rig
memories.body: Following three competing quotes, the board approved a £24,000 contract with Stage Electrics of Bristol to replace the Main House's 1998 tungsten rig with a 96-channel LED system. Technical manager Dave Holt pushed for Stage Electrics over the cheaper local firm because of their five-year parts warranty and same-day call-out clause, given how often the old dimmer racks tripped during last winter's panto. Installation was scheduled for the dark week between the Tempest closing and the next get-in, with electricians booked for four days. The old rig will be stripped out and sold for scrap or partial resale to a fringe venue in Leeds. Dave flagged that the changeover leaves no slack if delivery slips, since the following show's technical rehearsals are booked immediately after.

memories.subject: Director Tom Ellery cast for studio revival of The Weir in Studio 1

Cast comprises four company regulars and one guest actor from Leeds Playhouse, chosen for the piece's demand for naturalistic Irish accents; a dialect coach has been booked for two sessions at £300 each. The production budget of £11,000 is modest by main house standards, reflecting the 90-seat studio configuration. Ellery specifically requested minimal set changes between scenes to protect a tight technical schedule, since Studio 1 shares crew with the Main House during this period. Marketing has been asked to target the theatre's older, drama-literate subscriber base rather than family audiences.

Ellery raised concerns that the dialect coach's second session had to be cut entirely to claw back time. memories.subject: FOH manager Karen Voss introduces structured usher induction pack

Karen trialled the induction with the latest cohort of six volunteer ushers in November, running two-hour sessions in the Green Room on a Tuesday evening. memories.subject: Northern Spirit Co. signs £5,000 bar spirits supply deal

memories.subject: Northern Spirit Co. delivery mix-up leaves bar short over opening weekend
memories.body:
The first Northern Spirit Co. delivery arrived with only 15 of the 40 bottles ordered, after a warehouse picking error substituted cases of the standard gin for the promised spiced rum variant meant to launch alongside the Christmas production's opening weekend. With three sold-out performances and no reserve stock, the bar ran out of the advertised seasonal cocktail by the Saturday matinee interval, prompting refunds for four pre-ordered interval drinks packages. Northern Spirit Co. apologised and expedited a replacement delivery within 48 hours, plus offered a 10% credit against the next invoice. The bar manager has asked for a written stock-confirmation email before all future deliveries during peak weeks, and is reviewing whether Th'Real Ale Co.'s more reliable delivery pattern should be used as the template for supplier agreements going forward.

memories.subject: Boiler service contract renewed with Northgate Mechanical for Coach House

memories.subject: Box office manager Ruth Aldous flags Spektrix reporting gaps post-migration
memories.body: Ruth Aldous has raised concerns with the Spektrix account manager about missing historical sales data following the system migration, on top of the duplicate booking glitch already experienced during the panto on-sale. Three years of audience demographic data from the old system did not transfer cleanly, complicating the audience development report due to Arts Council England as part of National Portfolio reporting requirements. Aldous estimates it will take two to three weeks of manual reconciliation using archived spreadsheets to rebuild accurate figures. Spektrix has offered a discounted support package to assist, and Aldous has asked the board to consider this cost, roughly £600, as a necessary one-off given the scale of the funding uplift now riding on accurate reporting.

memories.subject: Trustee Ian Fothergill's catering conflict prompts review of supplier policy
memories.body: Following Ian Fothergill's declared conflict of interest over the catering contract, the board has commissioned a review of its supplier procurement policy, to be led by new finance trustee Fiona Marsh. The review will examine whether existing arrangements, including the Th'Real Ale Co. sponsorship and the Northern Spirit Co. spirits deal, were properly tendered and declared. Marsh has requested sight of all supplier contracts signed in the past two years before the March AGM, given existing concerns about trustee attendance levels raised for that meeting. Fothergill has recused himself from catering-related votes pending the outcome, and the board chair has asked for a written policy draft by January so it can be adopted before any renewal of the current catering arrangement, which expires in April.

memories.subject: Grace Oduya's contract extension revisited amid touring rehearsal clash
memories.body: Following the clash between Grace Oduya's touring dates and her monologue evening rehearsal block, Priya Chandrasekaran has convened a scheduling meeting with company stage manager Dave Holt to revisit the terms of Oduya's three-year contract extension. Oduya is contracted for the Hobson's Choice tour's four venues through late November, overlapping with the compressed rehearsal period Holt engineered to save the monologue evening's opening after the earlier Ellis Wing reshuffle. Options discussed include recasting the monologue evening's second act reading to a covering actor, or delaying its press night by one week. Chandrasekaran is reluctant to delay given marketing materials are already printed, but recognises Oduya's touring commitment was agreed before the monologue evening was programmed. A decision is expected by the end of the week.

memories.subject: Ridgeway Signs commissioned for spring season lamp-post banners
memories.body: Marketing officer Della Frear placed an order with Ridgeway Signs of Harrowgate for twenty double-sided lamp-post banners along Market Street, advertising the spring season including Priya Chandrasekaran's first full programmed run. Cost came to £1,340 including installation and removal, agreed against the marketing budget line rather than the general publicity pot, since the board had flagged in January that street presence was underused compared to neighbouring Dalesbridge Playhouse. Artwork was signed off by Della on 12 February, with Ridgeway quoting a three-week turnaround from proof approval to installation, timed to go up ten days before the spring brochure mailing landed with Friends of Harrowgate Rep members. Della noted this was the first time the theatre had used lamp-post banners rather than shop-window posters for a season launch.

Ridgeway Signs missed their quoted installation date for the Market Street lamp-post banners, citing a printer fault at their Leeds workshop; banners intended to go up ten days before the spring on-sale instead arrived four days after tickets went live on Spektrix. Della Frear complained that the delay undercut the whole point of street advertising timed to the brochure mailing, and asked for a partial refund on the £1,340 invoice, which Ridgeway offered as a 15% discount rather than cash back. memories.subject: Digital archive project awarded ACE Develop Your Creative Practice funding
memories.body: The theatre's application to Arts Council England's Develop Your Creative Practice fund for a digital archive project, cataloguing forty years of programme notes, production photographs and posters from the Harrowgate Rep back-stock, was awarded £6,500 in November. The scheme, proposed by former literary associate Hannah Riggs before she left in September, aims to digitise material currently stored in cardboard boxes in the Coach House Wing attic and make it searchable online for schools and researchers. The grant covers a part-time archivist for four months and scanning equipment hire from a Leeds supplier. Executive director Neil Bramwell welcomed the award as a rare piece of good funding news alongside the tighter core Arts Council uplift, though he noted delivery would depend on finding suitable freelance cover given current staff capacity.

memories.subject: Digital archive project stalled by marketing officer capacity shortage
memories.body:
The £6,500 digital archive project has stalled three months into its four-month window because Della Frear, who absorbed archivist-liaison duties after Hannah Riggs's departure, has been unable to free up time alongside the spring banner campaign and ongoing Spektrix reporting fixes. No freelance archivist has yet been recruited despite the grant covering the post, as two candidates withdrew after being offered only a short fixed-term contract. Neil Bramwell has written to Arts Council England requesting a two-month extension to the funding period rather than risk clawback, explaining the delay honestly as a staffing capacity issue rather than project abandonment. Della has asked the board to consider whether archive cataloguing should sit with a volunteer or trainee post longer term, rather than being bolted onto the marketing role again.

memories.subject: New under-26 concessionary ticket tier launched at £8 a seat
memories.body: Box office manager Ruth Aldous introduced a flat £8 concessionary ticket price for under-26s across all main house productions from the spring season onward, replacing the previous ad hoc student-rush arrangement that only applied to unsold seats on the day. The new tier is bookable in advance through Spektrix, aimed at building younger audiences ahead of Priya Chandrasekaran's programming shift toward newer writing. Ruth reported uptake of around 60 tickets in the first fortnight, modest but encouraging given no dedicated marketing push yet. The tier was costed to reduce average per-seat yield by roughly £4 compared with standard concessions, absorbed within projected uplift from the new Spektrix system's better upsell prompts at checkout. Audience development committee will review uptake figures at the June board meeting.

memories.subject: Bar switches crisp and snack supplier to Yorkshire Crisp Co
memories.body: The bar has moved its crisps and bar-snack supply from national brand Tayto to independent Yorkshire Crisp Co, based twenty miles away in Ripon, after Tayto's wholesale price rose 18% in October. Bar manager Colin Whitfield negotiated a standing order of forty cases a month at a discount for regular volume, and reports customer feedback has been positive, with several patrons commenting favourably on the locally-sourced angle, which chimes with the earlier switch to Fox & Bean coffee. Margins improved slightly, by around 3p a packet, though Colin flagged that Yorkshire Crisp Co cannot yet match Tayto's range of flavours, meaning cheese and onion sometimes sells out on busy Saturday nights before the interval rush.

memories.subject: Saturday Youth Theatre performer Jasmine Cole cast in touring ensemble
memories.body: Sixteen-year-old Jasmine Cole, a four-year member of the Saturday Youth Theatre under Sian Vaughan, has been cast in a small ensemble role in the touring production, becoming the first youth theatre alumna to appear in a main-stage professional show at Harrowgate Rep. Sian described it as validation of the programme's move toward more ambitious devised work, and Jasmine will rehearse alongside the adult company during half-term while continuing her GCSEs. Her school, St Aidan's Secondary, has agreed a flexible attendance arrangement to accommodate rehearsal days. Marcus Webb, who tutors the devising strand, said Jasmine's casting has already prompted enquiries from three younger members hoping for similar opportunities, and Sian is considering whether to formalise a youth-to-company pathway scheme for next season.

memories.subject: Board approves new trustee expenses policy after AGM attendance concerns
memories.body: Following discussions about trustee attendance and engagement raised ahead of the AGM, the board approved a formal trustee expenses policy at its February meeting, covering travel mileage at 45p per mile, overnight accommodation for trustees travelling from outside the district, and a cap of £150 per quarter without prior chair approval. Chair Robert Denholm proposed the policy partly to remove ambiguity that had contributed to informal grumbling among trustees about unequal treatment, and partly in response to the governance review that recommended clearer financial procedures generally. The policy was passed unanimously, with treasurer input on how expense claims should be logged against the same reporting system used for core financial oversight. memories.subject: November storm floods Coach House scenery dock loading bay
memories.body: On the night of 14 November the gale that hit the market town drove rainwater under the loading bay doors of the Coach House scenery dock, submerging the floor to a depth of roughly four inches before the overnight duty technician noticed and raised the alarm. Three MDF flats built for the spring season and a stack of six rostra units were damaged beyond repair, along with a pallet of timber offcuts kept for quick repairs. Estimated cost of replacement materials came to £2,400. The technical manager has asked estates to fit raised door thresholds and a sump pump before winter, since the dock sits below street level and has flooded twice in five years. Building committee to review at next meeting.

memories.subject: Freelance sound designer Priti Nair contracted for Sleeping Beauty panto score

Nair is bringing in her regular collaborator, a percussionist, for two recording sessions rather than using stock library cues, which the production manager felt would lift the show given last year's mixed reviews on the panto's sound quality. memories.subject: Marketing officer Dan Pryce relaunches subscriber e-newsletter on Substack

memories.subject: Volunteer garden group maintains rear courtyard beds and planters

The group meets Wednesday mornings and has planted herbs, including rosemary and mint, which the bar has started using as garnishes for its gin serves. Sutcliffe has asked the building committee for a small budget, around £150 a year, for compost and bulbs, and for a lockable shed to store tools currently kept in a corridor near the stage door, which fire officers noted as a minor obstruction during the last inspection.

Early results for the first month show a rise to roughly 58% average occupancy, though staff note some of this may be displaced bookings from Wednesday and Thursday performances rather than genuinely new audience. The offer will run for one full season before being reviewed, with marketing asked to promote it specifically to the under-served commuter-town audience rather than existing subscribers, to avoid simply discounting tickets already likely to sell.

memories.subject: Yorkshire Dairy Ices signed for interval ice cream concession

memories.subject: Resident actor Owen Pike cast as Mickey in autumn Blood Brothers revival

memories.subject: Cussins Fire Safety flags stalls carpet as fire risk during September inspection
memories.body: The annual fire safety inspection carried out by Cussins Fire Safety on 3 September identified the Main House stalls carpet, laid in 1998 and never replaced, as failing current flame-retardancy standards under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order. Inspector Dave Holroyd noted visible wear across rows F to K, 340-seat capacity affected, and recommended replacement within twelve months rather than immediate closure, given the carpet's current condition does not yet constitute an active hazard. The report has been logged with building manager Terry Whitfield and forwarded to the board's health and safety subcommittee. Cussins has also flagged the need for updated emergency lighting certification in the Coach House scenery dock, unrelated to the carpet finding, to be actioned separately before the winter season begins.

Treasurer Fiona Marsh proposed phasing the carpet work in two halves, stalls first then circle, to spread cost across two accounting years, but building manager Terry Whitfield warned partial replacement may not satisfy the twelve-month compliance deadline set by inspector Dave Holroyd. memories.subject: NPO 2024-27 renewal application submitted with revised artistic plan
memories.body: Executive Director Miriam Cross submitted the theatre's National Portfolio Organisation renewal application to Arts Council England on 30 June, requesting £285,000 in annual core funding for the 2024-27 cycle, an increase of £22,000 on the current settlement. memories.subject: NPO renewal decision delay forces finance subcommittee to model cashflow gap

Treasurer discussions on 20 November also raised the possibility of a short-term loan from the theatre's reserve-holding charitable trust if the overdraft extension is declined. Executive Director Miriam Cross has asked box office manager Ruth Aldous to expedite December ticket revenue reporting to strengthen the case presented to the bank.

memories.subject: Coach House courtyard composting scheme launched for bar food waste

The bins sit adjacent to the volunteer garden group's planters, and coordination between the two groups over access timing was agreed at a September meeting. memories.subject: Story Seeds early years workshop partnership launched with St Chad's Primary

The scheme is separate from Sian Vaughan's teenage Untold Histories strand but sits under the same youth programme budget line, with a modest £1,200 allocation drawn from unrestricted reserves rather than a grant. memories.subject: Trustee Malcolm Webb elected board chair after Whitfield resignation
memories.body: Following Sheila Whitfield's resignation for health reasons after five years as chair, the board elected trustee Malcolm Webb unopposed at the January meeting. His election was welcomed given ongoing concerns about deferred maintenance costs across the Grade II listed building, an area where his professional background is seen as directly useful. memories.subject: Grade II listed Green Room ceiling survey uncovers dry rot damage
memories.body: Structural surveyor Colin Marsh (Marsh & Yates Conservation) inspected the Green Room ceiling on 14 March after staff reported a musty smell and sagging plaster. His report, delivered 2 April, confirmed active dry rot in the joists above the fireplace, likely linked to a slow leak from the roof valley last repaired in 2019. Estimated remedial cost is £22,000, requiring removal of listed cornicing under Historic England guidance. The board's buildings subcommittee agreed to close the Green Room from 10 April pending scaffolding access, redirecting green-room functions (cast warm-up, small meetings) elsewhere in the building. memories.subject: ACE Elevate award of £18,000 secured for ticketing system overhaul

The award letter, received 6 May, stipulates the funds must be spent by March next year and requires a short case study on audience data use for ACE's regional bulletin. Ruth Aldous has flagged that the delay leaves existing Spektrix reporting gaps unresolved through the busy panto booking period, when accurate real-time sales data matters most. The finance subcommittee will review contingency options in September, including switching to an alternative supplier, Datapos, at a slightly higher unit cost, to avoid losing the grant altogether.

memories.subject: Spring tour cast reshuffled after lead actor ankle injury
memories.body: Lead actor Priya Anand sustained a sprained ankle during a technical rehearsal on 3 September, three days before the Dales Touring Network's autumn swap opened at Ilkley Playhouse. Understudy Ffion Pryce stepped into the role for the first four performances while Anand underwent physiotherapy, with the production's fight and movement director revising choreography to remove a staircase descent flagged as high risk. Anand returned to the role on 8 September for the remaining tour dates, though the company stage manager has since built a standing understudy rehearsal into the schedule for future tours as a precaution. The theatre's insurer was notified as a precaution, though no claim was made since Anand's absence was under the five-day threshold requiring formal reporting.

Chair Malcolm Webb has asked the nominations committee to identify a replacement with marketing or audience development experience before the fund-raising strategy is finalised in the autumn. memories.subject: Bar introduces low-alcohol range after customer feedback survey

Early sales figures for the September to November period show low-alcohol options accounting for roughly 6% of bar takings on performance nights, higher than anticipated among the under-30 audience segment identified in the under-26 concession scheme. memories.subject: Youth Theatre launches Saturday drama club for children aged six to eight

Youth and Community Officer Beth Naylor is leading the sessions, supported by two Youth Theatre alumni employed as paid assistants at £11 an hour. Initial uptake was strong, with 14 children enrolled against a planned cap of 16, largely through word of mouth rather than formal marketing. The bursary scheme already in place for low-income families has been extended to cover this younger group, and the education team is monitoring whether the new club increases retention into the main Youth Theatre programme once children turn nine.

memories.subject: Main House orchestra pit lift jams mid-run during Blood Brothers tech week
memories.body: On 14 October the hydraulic pit lift stalled halfway during the Wednesday tech rehearsal for Blood Brothers, trapping three musicians below stage level for twenty minutes. Technical manager rang Stagetech Hire Ltd, who supplied a temporary scaffold platform overnight at a cost of £1,150 to keep the band visible for press night. The original mechanism, installed in 1998, has not been serviced since 2019. Production manager noted the fault in the incident log and flagged it to the board's buildings subcommittee, since the pit is also used by touring companies under the Dales Touring Network swap. Owen Pike's cast were rescheduled around the stoppage, losing a full run-through. A full inspection by the original manufacturer has been booked for early November before the show opens to the public.

memories.subject: Ecology survey finds pipistrelle bat roost in Coach House roof void
memories.body: Ahead of scheduled gutter clearance, ecologist Fiona Marsh of Pennine Ecology Ltd surveyed the Coach House roof void on 3 September and confirmed an active pipistrelle bat roost in the eastern rafters, with droppings consistent with maternity use over several seasons. The survey was commissioned after Northern Roofworks flagged blocked valley gutters nearby and asked whether works could proceed unimpeded. Because pipistrelles are a protected species, the report recommends no roof disturbance between May and August and suggests a European Protected Species licence may be required from Natural England before any works touching the roof timbers. The Coach House also houses the scenery dock, so touring get-ins have continued unaffected for now, but the finding has been logged against the building condition survey chair Malcolm Webb commissioned earlier this year.

memories.subject: Winter Kestrel tour adds fourth venue at Skipton's Century Theatre
memories.body: The Dales Touring Network has agreed to add Skipton's Century Theatre as a fourth stop for the winter tour of Ellen Braithwaite's adaptation of A Kestrel for a Knave, extending the tour by four performances across the second week of February. Touring coordinator Jan Fowles negotiated a reduced hire fee of £850 per night in exchange for Harrowgate providing get-in labour, since Skipton's technical staff are limited to one full-time employee. The addition brings projected touring income to £14,600 against a £11,200 transport and accommodation cost, an improvement on previous tour margins. Artistic director Ruth Calloway supported the addition partly because Skipton has a strong existing schools relationship that may feed into future youth outreach bookings, though the get-in schedule now requires an extra minibus run that wasn't in the original touring budget.

memories.subject: Skipton stage floor unsuitable for Kestrel set, floor covering hired
memories.body:
A site visit ahead of the Skipton Century Theatre date on the Kestrel tour found the venue's original 1930s sprung stage floor too uneven for the raked platform used in the production's design, risking damage to both the set and the floor itself. Set designer Colm Whelan specified a temporary Marley dance floor covering, hired from Harlequin Floors at a cost of £480 for the week, to be laid and struck by the touring crew on the get-in day. This added roughly ninety minutes to an already tight get-in schedule and required renegotiation of the crew call time with Skipton's venue manager. Touring coordinator Jan Fowles has flagged that the floor survey should have been done before the venue was confirmed, and has proposed adding a mandatory technical site visit to the tour-booking checklist for all future non-standard venues.

memories.subject: Board approves 2025 ticket price rise of one pound across all bands
memories.body: At the November board meeting, trustees approved a £1 increase across all Main House ticket price bands for the 2025 season, raising the top price from £24 to £25 and the concession rate from £14 to £15, the first rise since 2022. Treasurer Alison Reed presented the case as necessary to offset a projected £9,000 shortfall in box office income against rising production costs, while chair Malcolm Webb pushed for the increase to be modest to avoid deterring the midweek Tuesday two-for-one audience. The rise takes effect from the spring Rebecca adaptation onward, with existing group bookings and school matinees exempted until September 2025. Marketing manager Fran Duckworth was asked to review whether the increase should be publicised ahead of time or absorbed quietly into the spring brochure pricing.

memories.subject: Student ticket uptake falls after price rise, box office reviews concession band

Denise flagged that the new £15 concession price sits close to the full adult Tuesday two-for-one rate, making the standard concession less attractive than the midweek offer for students who can travel flexibly. She has proposed a separate £10 under-25 rate for Wednesday and Thursday performances only, to be trialled during the Kestrel winter run, and has asked treasurer Alison Reed whether this can be modelled without breaching the income targets set when the price rise was agreed.

memories.subject: Bar switches till roll supplier after national paper shortage
memories.body: The bar's regular till roll supplier, Ripon Office Supplies, was unable to fulfil orders for six weeks in October due to a national thermal paper shortage, forcing bar manager Callum Reid to source emergency stock from a Leeds cash-and-carry at nearly double the usual unit cost. To avoid a repeat, Callum has switched the bar's ongoing supply contract to Yorkshire Paper Products, who guaranteed continuity through a standing monthly order of forty rolls at £38, slightly higher than the previous rate but with a written supply guarantee. The switch was approved by general manager Sue Ellerby without board sign-off as it fell within Callum's existing procurement authority. The shortage briefly affected the SumUp card readers' paper receipt printing at both the bar and the ice cream concession stand during the busiest weekend of the autumn run.

memories.subject: Two former Youth Theatre members return as paid workshop assistants
memories.body: Youth Theatre director Hannah Griggs has taken on two former members, eighteen-year-old Callie Marsh and nineteen-year-old Tomasz Wysocki, as paid assistant workshop leaders for the Saturday drama club sessions, at £11 an hour for four hours a week each. Both completed the summer intensive in previous years and have since gone on to drama courses at Leeds and Huddersfield respectively. Hannah proposed the appointments to the board's youth subcommittee as a low-cost way of increasing adult-to-child ratios following the safeguarding policy tightening, without the expense of hiring additional qualified staff. Both assistants have undergone updated DBS checks and safeguarding training before starting. Hannah hopes the arrangement will also create a visible progression route for current members, and has asked whether a similar paid assistant role could be created for the spring open day next year.

memories.subject: Ellis Wing rehearsal room boiler fails, electric heaters hired as stopgap
memories.body: The 1930s gas boiler serving the Ellis Wing offices and rehearsal room three failed overnight on 4 December, leaving staff working in coats until engineer Dave Sutcliffe of Sutcliffe Heating diagnosed a cracked heat exchanger beyond economic repair. Building manager Terry Holt authorised hire of four Rhino R110 electric heaters from Selby Plant Hire at £180 a week to keep rehearsals running for the Kestrel tour cast, who use room three daily. Sutcliffe quoted £6,400 for a like-for-like replacement but warned parts lead time is eight weeks. Terry flagged the Ellis Wing has no separate zone valve, so any permanent fix will also need pipework isolating from the Green Room's dry rot repair area, adding cost. Interim decision: heaters stay until January, replacement deferred to the new financial year.

The subcommittee agreed to bring the boiler forward against the pit lift bid, funding it from the maintenance reserve rather than waiting for the new financial year, on condition Sutcliffe confirms a firm installation date before the Kestrel tour returns from Skipton over half term.

memories.subject: Local writer Sadie Marlowe commissioned to adapt Dick Whittington for Christmas show
memories.body: Harrowgate Rep commissioned local writer Sadie Marlowe to adapt Dick Whittington as its December family show, her first full-length commission after two youth theatre scripts. Contract signed in June for a £4,500 fee plus royalty share, first draft due 1 September. The artistic director wants a northern-set version, relocating the story to a fictional mill town rather than London, with a rescued cat puppet built by the props workshop. The casting brief calls for a strong panto dame and a live three-piece band rather than backing tracks, a departure from previous years' recorded score. Budget set at £22,000, higher than 2023's panto because of the puppet build and band fees, agreed by the board in July as the show is expected to be the season's strongest earner, historically selling to 85% capacity across its three-week run.

memories.subject: Dick Whittington dame recast after Colin Ashworth's commercial booking clashes
memories.body:
Resident actor Colin Ashworth, cast as the dame in Sadie Marlowe's new Dick Whittington adaptation, withdrew in October after his voiceover agency booked him for a six-week beer commercial clashing with the show's five-week rehearsal block starting 11 November. The casting director offered the role to Nadia Osei, who accepted on reduced rehearsal time, working evenings with dame costume fittings moved to Studio 2 to avoid clashing with the Kestrel wardrobe calls already using that space. Marlowe rewrote two dame scenes to soften physical comedy business Ashworth had developed with the director, unwilling to assume it would transfer to Osei's performance style. memories.subject: Foyer CCTV extended after ticket-fraud incidents at Saturday matinees

memories.subject: Youth Theatre technical crew scheme partners with Harrowgate College on AV training

The scheme runs Thursday evenings from January to March, culminating in students running get-in and cues for the Youth Theatre's own spring showcase rather than relying on staff. The college contributed £600 toward radio headsets, while the theatre covered DBS checks and the public liability extension needed for under-18s working near the grid. Installation by Hearing Solutions Yorkshire is booked for the dark week between the Kestrel tour's return and the Christmas show get-in, so as not to disrupt performances. memories.subject: Outdoor Midsummer Night's Dream staged in Coach House courtyard this July

Bar staff will run a small outdoor servery from the Coach House annex doors. memories.subject: Resident actor Marcus Fielding takes ensemble and movement captain role in Kestrel
memories.body: Marcus Fielding, now in his third season with the resident company, has been cast in the ensemble of A Kestrel for a Knave and asked to serve as movement captain, working with director Ellen Braithwaite's choreographer to stage the kestrel-flying sequence using aerial silk rigging borrowed from a Leeds circus school. His contract has been extended by two weeks to cover the additional rehearsal call for rigging safety training, run by an external aerial coach at a day rate of £180. memories.subject: Youth Theatre alumni panel formed to advise board on programme direction
memories.body: Six former Youth Theatre members, aged nineteen to twenty-four, have been convened into an informal alumni advisory panel meeting quarterly with the youth programme coordinator, following requests at last year's summer intensive for more say in workshop content. Two panel members, Chloe Ibbotson and Dan Renshaw, have also been taken on as paid workshop assistants this term. memories.subject: Bar switches real ale supplier from Dalesbrew to Ilkley Brewery over delivery gaps
memories.body: The bar has moved its cask ale supply from Dalesbrew to Ilkley Brewery after three missed Thursday deliveries this spring left the bar dry ahead of weekend performances. Bar manager Colin Ashworth's deputy, who handles ordering, says Ilkley Brewery has committed to a standing Tuesday delivery slot and matched Dalesbrew's trade pricing. Dalesbrew's sponsorship of the season brochure is unaffected and remains separate from the cask supply arrangement, though the switch has been noted informally as awkward given the sponsorship relationship. The bar retains one Dalesbrew seasonal ale on rotation as a goodwill gesture. Stock records show the changeover saved an estimated four wasted trading nights compared with the previous quarter.

memories.subject: Board holds strategic away-day at Coach House on five-year building plan
memories.body: The full board met for a Saturday away-day on 9 March in the Coach House annex, facilitated by chair Geoff Marsden, to sketch a five-year capital plan spanning the roof, chimney, fire stairs and pit lift works currently competing for limited reserves. Trustee Alison Reed presented a simplified cash-flow model showing the theatre cannot fund more than one major capital item per year without a dedicated appeal. The day produced a rough priority order, though no formal vote, and agreed that Terry Holt's competing bids should be brought together into a single ranked capital register rather than assessed piecemeal. Newly recruited trustees attended as observers ahead of formal AGM confirmation, giving early exposure to the scale of the maintenance backlog.

memories.subject: Dialect coach Priya Nair booked for Kestrel's Yorkshire vernacular work
memories.body: Ellen Braithwaite's adaptation of A Kestrel for a Knave leans heavily on South Yorkshire dialect, and after a read-through in November the director felt the cast's accents were inconsistent, particularly among actors drafted in from outside the region. Voice and dialect coach Priya Nair, who previously worked on a Sheffield Crucible production, has been booked for four sessions across December at a day rate of £280, covering both the Harrowgate cast and the understudies. Sessions are scheduled in Studio 1 rather than Studio 2, which remains occupied by wardrobe fittings displaced from the Green Room. Nair will also record reference audio for cast members to rehearse against independently, since full-company dialect calls are hard to schedule around the Rebecca tour clash affecting the lead.

memories.subject: Sound engineer Dave Kirby departs after eleven years, freelance cover booked
memories.body: Dave Kirby, resident sound engineer since 2013, has left to take a permanent post at Leeds Playhouse, giving six weeks' notice in October. Rather than recruit a new permanent post before the winter season, technical manager Rob Ashby has booked freelancer Callum Reece to cover the Kestrel run and into the Dick Whittington get-in, at £180 per day plus mileage from Bradford. Reece has worked the venue before as a dep during Blood Brothers and knows the Main House desk, but has raised concerns about the age of the analogue mixing console, which has been unreliable since a fader fault appeared last spring. Ashby has asked Reece to log any further faults in writing so they can be raised with the finance subcommittee.

Reece has submitted a written fault log, as agreed with Rob Ashby, and is now formally requesting the theatre budget for a replacement digital desk rather than continue running repairs, estimating a mid-range Allen & Heath model at around £4,200. Ashby has forwarded the request to the finance subcommittee alongside the existing Ellis Wing boiler and fire stairs bids, noting that further show-stopping failures during a paying performance would be worse publicity than the capital outlay. memories.subject: Touring merchandise stall trialled at Skipton's Century Theatre for Kestrel dates

This is the first time Harrowgate Rep has run merchandise off-site rather than only at the home venue, and Pickersgill is treating it as a pilot ahead of the proposed Sheffield Library Theatre date. Staffing is being covered by two front-of-house volunteers travelling with the touring van, with float and takings reconciled against the home box office's Spektrix system nightly by phone. memories.subject: Coach House annex roof leak damages stored touring flats ahead of spring

Several painted flats from the spring tour's get-in stock were water-damaged, along with two crates of props not yet unpacked from the autumn season. Building manager Terry Holt has logged this as separate from the known pipistrelle roost issue in the same roof void, since the leak is on the opposite slope, but it complicates timing given the Natural England licence delay already holding up wider roof works. Replacement of the damaged flats is estimated at £600 in materials and carpenter time, and an insurance claim is being prepared.

memories.subject: Board opens early discussion on artistic director succession ahead of 2026
memories.body: With artistic director Simon Wray's contract due to end in summer 2026, the board used part of its strategic away-day at the Coach House to open informal discussion on succession planning, three years out from the deadline in order to allow time for a considered recruitment process. Chair Diane Ferrow noted the theatre cannot afford the disruption of a rushed appointment given recent turnover, including trustee Margaret Voss's resignation and ongoing finance pressures. No formal timetable was set, but it was agreed Wray should be consulted directly early in 2025 about his own intentions, and that a small trustee working group, excluding any newly recruited business trustees, would scope the process before it goes to full board.

memories.subject: Costume workshop delay pushes Seagull dress run to Thursday

Original leadwork is being recast rather than replaced, per conservation officer Diane Ashby's condition, and glass panes are being reset in situ to preserve the original wave distortion. Scaffolding is up on the north elevation only, leaving the south side accessible for the spring school matinees.
